mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces wage growth and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which increases input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods compared to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that increases uncertainty and discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of co-triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 12-month MA AND HOUST < 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market that boosts wage pressure and input costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND UNRATE < 4.0% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between the real savings rate (RSAFS divided by GDPC1) and S&P 500 forward returns over a 5-day horizon, such that higher household saving implies greater future investment and economic growth, driving positive returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between the real savings rate and 5-day forward S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) in out-of-sample tests.
